caption:
A New York startup launched an AI ad platform 3 days ago and there's zero pricing page yet — here's why I'm still paying attention.

AdAI came out of Revolution Venture Studios on September 11, 2026, and it's doing something different from the flood of "type a prompt, get an ad" tools that came before it. Instead of generic prompts, it uses AI agents that pull from your actual brand assets — logos, past creative, product shots — and your brand guidelines, then output finished image AND video ads. Not drafts. Finished.

The idea: less "generate 50 random options and pick one," more "automated version of your in-house creative team that already knows your brand."

Here's my honest take: this thing is 3 days old. No independent hands-on reviews exist yet. No confirmed public pricing. No track record on whether the output is actually usable without heavy editing, which is where a lot of early ad-AI tools fall apart in month one. I'm flagging this as one to watch, not a tool I'm telling you to buy today.

If you run paid social or manage a brand's ad creative and you're tired of prompt-engineering your way to something on-brand, this is worth putting on your radar and checking back on in a month once real users have put it through its paces.

slides.heading: What AdAI actually is
slides.body: A New York startup incubated by Revolution Venture Studios, using AI agents (not one generative model) to build finished ad creative.

slides.heading: Not another prompt generator
slides.body: Instead of "type a prompt, get an image," it pulls from your existing brand assets — logos, product shots, past creative — and your brand guidelines.

slides.heading: Image AND video, same workflow
slides.body: Most tools split these. AdAI generates both static ads and video ads from one process, aiming for ready-to-publish output, not rough drafts.

slides.heading: Who backs it matters
slides.body: Revolution Venture Studios' incubation model suggests structured go-to-market support — relevant if you're betting on this tool sticking around.

slides.heading: The catch: no pricing, no reviews yet
slides.body: Zero public self-serve pricing as of launch. No independent hands-on reviews of output quality. This is early access territory, not a proven track record.

slides.heading: My honest verdict
slides.body: Watch this one, don't commit budget yet. Early ad-AI tools often struggle with brand consistency in month one — give it time before you rely on it.
